items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the provision of certain
professional services to children's camps and camps for children with
developmental disabilities
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4345

SPONSOR: BROUK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to the provision of
certain professional services to children's camps and camps for children
with developmental disabilities

 
PURPOSE:

The bill allows children's overnight camps, summer day camps, traveling
summer day camps and camps for children with developmental disabilities
to employ certain specified licensed professionals and mental healthcare
practitioners, in order to better serve the mental and physical needs of
these children during their summer camp experience.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends public health law section 1394(1) to
provide the public health and health planning council shall prescribe
standards and regulations for children's overnight, summer day and trav-
eling summer camps.

Section 2 amends public health law section 1394(3) to authorize the
operator of a children's overnight, summer day, or traveling summer day
camp, with a permit pursuant to public health law section 1393, to
employ or contract with the licensed professionals listed, to provide
professional services, provided all decisions, identification or coordi-
nation of these services, or other professional interactions with camp-
ers and staff at the camp are made based on the professional judgment of
such licensee within his or her lawful scope of practice for the purpose
of treating campers and staff during their attendance or employment at
such camp, pursuant to applicable regulations promulgated by the commis-
sioner in consultation with the commissioner of education.

Section 3 amends the public health law by adding two new sections 1394c
and 1394-d.

Public health law section 1394-c authorizes the operator of a children's
overnight, summer day, or traveling summer day camp, with a permit
pursuant to public health law section 1393, to employ or contract with
any of the mental health practitioners licensed under articles 153
(psychologists), 154 (social workers) and 163(mental health practition-
ers) of the education law, provided all decisions, identification or
coordination of these services, or other professional interactions with
campers and staff at the camp are made based on the professional judg-
ment of such licensee within his or her lawful scope of practice for the
purpose of treating campers and staff during their attendance or employ-
ment at such camp, pursuant to applicable regulations promulgated by the
commissioner in consultation with the commissioner of education.  Public
health law section 1394-d authorizes camps for children with disabili-
ties as defined in the New York codes, rules and regulations Title 10,
chapter 1, part 7-2.2, and in compliance with the justice center for the
protection of people with special needs, to employ or contract with any
of the licensed professionals under articles 132 (chiropractic), 135
(physical therapists),156 (occupational therapy), 159 (speech-language
pathologists and audiologists), 162 (athletic trainers) and 167 (applied
behavior analysis) of the education law, provided all decisions, iden-
tification or coordination of these services, or other professional
interactions with campers and staff at the camp are made based on the
professional judgment of such licensee within his or her lawful scope of
practice for the purpose of treating campers and staff during their
attendance or employment at such camp, pursuant to applicable regu-
lations promulgated by the commissioner in consultation with the commis-
sioner of education.

Section 4 is the effective date.

 
EXISTING LAW:

Under the current law, mental health professionals are excluded from the
list of permissible services a summer camp may engage on behalf of camp
attendees.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Parents and camps rely on the presence of licensed professionals and
practitioners to ensure the well-being of the children they serve.  Many
summer camps, if authorized, would employ additional licensed profes-
sionals and practitioners to provide needed services to care for the
mental health and physical well-being of campers. Under this legis-
lation, camps may choose to engage the services of social workers, phys-
ical therapists, psychologists, athletic trainers, mental health care
professionals, and occupational therapists.  Of particular note, camps
serving children affected by traumatic events would better meet the need
of campers by engaging licensed mental health practitioners. The signif-
icant increase in the number of young people diagnosed with mental
health disorders, coupled with the tragic increase in suicides among
young people, highlights the need for services by licensed mental health
practitioners. Although time at a summer camp is often considered a
vacation, mental health conditions do not take a vacation.

New York State has adopted the principle of parity between mental health
services and physical health services. This bill will further support
that principle.

Children at camps are disadvantaged when the law prohibits camps from
hiring professionals capable of addressing the physical and mental
health needs of campers. Camps must be permitted to offer services chil-
dren who need them during their summer camp experience. This legislation
provides peace of mind to parents, knowing that their children are in
the capable hands of licensed practitioners at summer camps.

 
LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: 53834 (Metzger) Passed Senate.

2018: S9072 (Ortt) - Referred to Rules/A11228 Abinanti - Referred to
Health.

2013-2014: S4108B (Bonacic) - Referred to Health/A6390B (Paulin) -
Referred to Codes.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None
 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
Immediately

AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the provision of certain

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S4345A

SPONSOR: BROUK
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the public health law, in relation to the provision of
certain professional services to children's camps and camps for children
with developmental disabilities

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

The bill would allow children's overnight camps, summer day camps, trav-
eling summer day camps and camps for children with developmental disa-
bilities to employ certain licensed professionals in order to better
serve the mental and physical needs of children during their summer camp
experience.

 
SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 of the bill amends public health law section 1394(1) to
provide the public health and health planning council shall prescribe
standards and regulations for children's overnight, summer day and trav-
eling summer camps.

Section 2 amends public health law section 1394(3) and adds new
provisions to authorize the operator of a children's overnight, summer
day, or traveling summer day camp, with a permit pursuant to public
health law section 1393, to employ or contract with the licensed profes-
sionals listed to provide professional services, and emergency medical
technicians to provide health services to assist the camp health direc-
tor, provided all decisions, identification or coordination of these
services, or other professional interactions with campers and staff at
the camp are made based on the professional judgment of such licensee
within his or her lawful scope of practice for the purpose of treating
campers and staff during their attendance or employment at such camp,
pursuant to applicable regulations promulgated by the commissioner in
consultation with the commissioner of education.

Section 3 amends the public health law by adding section 1394-c to
authorize camps for children with disabilities as defined in the New
York codes, rules and regulations Title 10, chapter 1, part 7-2.2, and
in compliance with the justice center for the protection of people with
special needs, to employ or contract with any of the licensed profes-
sionals under articles 132 (chiropractic), 136 (physical therapy), 156
(occupational therapy), 159 (speech-language pathologists and audiolo-
gists), 162 (athletic trainers) and 167 (applied behavior analysis) of
the education law, between June first and September fifteenth.

Section 4 is the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

Parents and camps rely on the presence of licensed professionals and
practitioners to ensure the well-being of the children they serve.  Many
summer camps, if authorized, would employ additional licensed profes-
sionals and practitioners to provide needed services for the mental
health and physical well-being of campers. Additionally, camps catering
to children whose lives have been impacted by traumatic events would be

better able to serve these children, by having licensed mental health
practitioners.

The significant increase in the number of young people diagnosed with
mental health disorders, coupled with the tragic increase in suicides
among our youth, highlights the need for continuous services by licensed
mental health practitioners. These mental health problems do not stop
when these children attend summer camps. In addition, New York State has
adopted the principal that there should be parity in the provision of
mental health services and physical health services.  This bill will
further support that principal.

Finally, children with developmental disabilities require additional
services that should be continued at camp. This bill will ensure that
the licensed professionals and practitioners needed to provide these
necessary services are available. Prohibiting children's camps from
hiring licensed professionals and practitioners specially trained to
deal with the physical and mental needs of the children they serve does
them a disservice. Camps should be allowed and encouraged to offer these
services to the children who need them during their summer camp experi-
ence.

This bill will provide peace of mind to parents, knowing that their
children are in the capable hands of licensed practitioners at summer
camp, while also allowing camps to provide the same nurturing services
that they have provided in the past.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-20: A.3074-A referred to higher education;
2018: A.11228 referred to health; same as S9072 (Ortt) referred to
Rules;
2016-17: A.9680-A referred to higher education; same as S.1603-A (Bona-
cic) passed senate;
2013-14: A.6360-B (Paulin) referred to health

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:

None.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect one year after it shall have become a law.

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 13  Chapter 289
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Senate Bill Number 4345-A, entitled:
 
    "AN ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to the provision
        of  certain  professional services to children's camps and camps
        for children with developmental disabilities"
 
    APPROVED
 
  I am in support of this legislation, which authorizes children's camps
to employ or  contract  with  licensed  psychologists,  social  workers,
mental  health  practitioners  and  behavior  analysts to provide mental
health services, and will aid these camps in meeting the needs of  their
campers and staff. The bill also allows camps for children with develop-
mental disabilities to hire licensed professionals, such as occupational
therapists  or  speech-language  pathologists,  to  provide professional
services.
 
  However, the legislation as written would prohibit  emergency  medical
technicians  (EMTs)  from acting as designated health directors. Because
smaller camps may be unable to afford  higher  level  licensure  profes-
sionals,  I  have reached an agreement with the Legislature to reinstate
the ability of EMTs to serve in this role. The agreement also  clarifies
that  the  services  may  be provided during the time a camp has a valid
permit to operate.
 
  On the basis of this agreement, this bill is approved.
 
  The bill is approved.                       (signed) ANDREW M. CUOMO
 
                                ______

summary: Authorizes summer camps to hire licensed social workers, physical therapists, psychologists, athletic trainers, mental health care professionals, occupational therapists and other licensed professionals to provide services.
